title: Product search response
description: What GET /rest/products/search?q=<text> answers with when the search succeeds. Only what the tests read is required, so a field the application adds later is not a failure here: the tests read id, name and price, and demanding the whole product would turn every product change into a red build for no reason.

status.description: A search that worked answers 'success' with the data below. A refused or failed call answers with an error envelope instead, which is a different response and is not what this schema describes.

data.description: The products that match the search. An empty array is a valid answer when nothing matches.

id.description: The number the application knows the product by, which is what a basket item is written with.

description.description: Free text, and it may hold the markup the shop renders with, so no pattern is put on it.

price.description: A price that lands on a whole number arrives as 2 and not as 2.0, which is why this is a number and not an integer.

createdAt.description: A timestamp the way the database writes it, for example '2026-10-04 00:11:52.012 +00:00'. That is why no 'date-time' format is claimed here: the format would be right and the values would still be refused.

deletedAt.description: Null for a product the shop still sells.
